name: Nested GG: Game Gear -> Master System
cli: brokendev.ps1 nested-everything gg2sms <in.gg> <out.sms> [-Profile <game id or file>] [-Feedback none|brokennes] [-Set key=value,...]
description: Static patching plus a small Z80 runtime: the GG-only ports ($00 Start/region, $01-$05 link, $06 stereo) and the GG's 12-bit colour writes are trapped and translated; the rest of the game runs unchanged on the SMS's identical Z80 and Mode 4 VDP. The dynamic pass (BrokenNes's GG core, headless) finds what a static scan cannot see.

settings.what: Where GG Start comes from: the SMS Pause button (NMI; on a Genesis in SMS mode, the pad's Start), buttons 1+2 held together, both, or never
How many reads of port $00 see Start held after one Pause press (Pause gives no release)
The region bit port $00 reports (auto: from the header, GG Japan -> japan)
GG 4-bit colour level -> SMS 2-bit level: nearest (0-2:0, 3-7:1, 8-12:2, 13-15:3) or the top two bits; a profile may give its own 16-entry list

The 256x192 SMS picture around the GG's 160x144 window: show what the game left in the name table (the GG view is already centred: columns 6-25, rows 3-20). Masking is not offered: the SMS can only blank 8 pixels on the left, and a line-interrupt letterbox would fight the game's own interrupt handler

How the runtime tells a colour-RAM select among control-port writes: heuristic (any byte with both top bits set; quickest, raster-safe), pairs (shadows the VDP's two-byte latch; a low address byte of $C0-$FF no longer fools it), status (pairs, and the status reads reset the shadow latch too; slowest)
OUT ($BE),A sites the dynamic pass never saw run: route them through the colour check (safe, slower) or leave them
Data-port sites seen writing only VRAM (tile uploads): leave them fast, or route them through the colour check too

profiles: BrokenDev/projects/nested-gg2sms/profiles/<game id>.json: settings, inputs (dynamic-pass scripts), ram, sites { "0x1234": "patch" | "leave" }, found (written by feedback)
